added_lines: matthew 22:34-40 when the pharisees heard that jesus had silenced the sadducees they got together and, to disconcert him , one of them put a question, ‘master, which is the greatest commandment of the law?’ jesus said, ‘you must love the lord your god with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. this is the greatest and the first commandment. the second r esembles it: you must love your neighbour as yourself. on these two commandments hang the whole law, and the prophets also .’.’ responsorial psalm . 17(18):2-4,47,51 i love you, lord, my strength. “you must love’” another group from the leadership of the jews seek to catch jesus out, the sadducees. jesus answers their question correctly by saying th at love of god comes before all else, how ever he also adds the second commandment, love your neig hbour as yourself. in this way jesus is telling us that to love god is to love one another. we cannot separate them. "if anyone says , 'i love god,' and yet hates his brother or sister, is a liar. for the person who does not love his brothe r or sister whom he has seen cannot love god whom he has not seen.". (1john 4:20). this love is not to be just words or mere talk but to be practical as we hear in the first reading for this sunday from the book of exodus. “ you must not molest the stranger or oppress him, you lived as strangers in the land of egypt. you must not be harsh with the widow, or with the orphan ” (ex22:20) memory is a very important part of our lives, it is important to recall who we are and where we come from. to love the stranger for the israelites is to remember that they were strangers in othe r lands in the past, and they know what it is not to belong. god has called us all into his family, we belong to him. while we can all be comfortable in belonging to a particular people and place and be wary of strangers, of people different to ourselves w hich can lead to segregation, racism, blaming stranger for everything, we as christians know that we are up of people from every nation and culture. our belonging is in christ and thus we are called to love one another as jesus loves us. welcoming to the stranger and to those in need. carrigtwohill

exploring the merging of diocese in the province of cashel at the request of the holy see, the bishops of irel and have been considering how our diocesan structures best serve our shared mission in the years ahead. this is not simply a question of boundaries, admini strative adjustments or the sharing of resources more effectively. primarily it is about we can better proclaim the gospel, support our clergy, relig ious and lay people, and strengthen our parishes and communities for evangelisation. as part of this discernment, the bishops of the cashel province considered a range of possible configurations. the following options are presented for further ref lection and consultation across the seven dioceses of the cashel province. 1. archdiocese of cashel and emly and diocese of limer ick merge. 2. archdiocese of cashel & emly, diocese of limerick a nd diocese of killaloe merge. 3. archdiocese of cashel and emly and waterford and lismore merge. 4. diocese of limerick and diocese of killaloe merge. 5. diocese of limerick and diocese of cloyne merge. 6. diocese of cork and ross and diocese of cloyne merge. 7. diocese of cloyne and the diocese of waterford and lismore merge. 8. diocese of kerry and diocese of limerick merge. 9. diocese of kerry and diocese of cloyne merge. 10. diocese of kerry and the diocese of cork and ross m erge. maintain the current diocesan structures – ruled out by the papal nuncio! these are not decisions or an agreed map f or the future, rather material for further discussion. as bishops, we recognise that dioceses are communities of faith with their own histories, relationships and traditions. any change must therefore be approached with prayer, sensitivity and care for the people and communities involved. synodal discernment also asks each of us to look be yond our own self-interests and to consider what will best serve the catholic church i n ireland and in particular munster as a whole. everyone in every parish is encourag ed to make their voice heard when opportunities for consultation are announced locally by their diocesan bishop. finally, we encourage everyone to actively engage i n this process, and to the keep this central question at the heart our prayer and reflec tion: how can we best equip the catholic church in munste r for mission, evangelisation and the service of god’s people? with every blessing, bishops of munster province world missions sunday : thank you for your support of mission sunday. if have notd onated before and you wish to do so or you may either donate over the phone (01) 497 2035 or on our website:
